verdict_reason: Wave 4 converged. It opened no family: all 8 dives revised existing families, and its 13 new MUST rules and all its new failure modes sit in those families. The three fleet config files are now assembled and watched (GO-GATE-22/23). The only two questions that were load-bearing and answerable now were answered during harvest by reading source: the ggcr layer context is fixed at remote.Image/remote.Layer time (image.go:154, layer.go:38-39, fetcher.go:323), and x/tools v0.50.0 toonew.go:28-29 excludes json/v2 from stdversion. They became authoring notes N-7 and N-8. Every other open question is one of three kinds: a dated go-upgrade re-check, a measurement the corpus cannot supply (Windows, macOS, GitHub OIDC, Bazel cross-platform), or an owner decision with its default applied.
frame_corrections: x/tools >= v0.50.0 excludes encoding/json/v2 and jsontext from stdversion (toonew.go:28-29). golangci-lint 2.14.0 and nogo both build against v0.50.0, so neither can catch the GO-LANG-04 violation. Bare go vet on go1.27.1 still catches it, because its vendored toonew.go:24-25 excludes only testing/synctest.

On go-containerregistry, a layer's request context is fixed when remote.Image/remote.Layer is called (image.go:154,272; layer.go:38-39; fetcher.go:323). The watchdog's WithCancelCause must be created before that call and passed via remote.WithContext.
QF1009 blocks under the fleet config; it is not a hint (C-22).
go test runs 12 of the 35 vet analyzers on go1.27.1, not 11 of 36 (C-25).
A unix build tag on the SDK signal classifier breaks the Windows build (GO-API-19).
ExitCode() is -1 for a signal death seen in-process, and 255 after a shell forwards it (GO-API-19).
Cmd.Wait returns the process error in preference to the copy error (exec.go:944-959), so the context cause must be checked before exit classification (GO-API-20).
ggcr's write path uses retry.Never, so WithRetryStatusCodes has no effect on writes (GO-NET-17 gap 4).
The dist CDN returns 200 for every user agent tested (GO-NET-18).
-buildvcs=true exits 0 on the golang/go#74763 layout, so an exit code does not prove stamping (GO-REL-03).
Bazel's default fastbuild strips binaries and -c opt does not (BZL-GO-15).
nogo passes the SDK's GoVersion rather than the module's go line, so stdversion is inert under nogo (BZL-GO-06/07).
A nested cobra group that is not sealed exits 0 on a typo (GO-CLI-21).
gopls v0.23.0 has a yield analyzer; vet and golangci-lint 2.14.0 have none (GO-LANG-08).
Interface methods never take type parameters, even on 1.27 (GO-LANG-23).
A generic type alias needs go 1.23, including cross-package use (GO-LANG-03).
nogreenteagc is still accepted on 1.27.1 and is a real opt-out (GO-OBS C9).
A runtime-sized make above 32 B heap-allocates even when -m reports 'does not escape' (GO-OBS C7/C8).
contradictions_across_consolidations: 1. GO-LANG-22 vs GO-GATE-09/13/22: GO-MOD-08 owns the depguard list. The list becomes 13 entries: its own 11, plus automaxprocs (GO-OBS-06), plus x/exp/constraints (GO-LANG-22). All three files re-quote it, then config verify, the superset check and L13 are re-run.

2. GO-LANG-08 vs GO-GATE-01: GO-LANG-08 owns the command. The gate gains conditional step 10: pinned gopls check, grepped for 'yield may be called again', run only where func(yield func( appears, and only on the stable leg.
3. GO-CONC-17 example vs GO-API-20: GO-API-20 wins (typed *TimeoutError cause). GO-CONC-17 keeps its mechanism and SHOULD severity, and swaps its example.
4. GO-IO-10 vs GO-API-20: GO-IO-10 keeps its text. Its verification cites GO-API-20's real-spawn case and requires checking the cause before exit classification.
5. GO-API line 63 (CLI opt-in to the overlay) vs GO-GATE-18/22: GO-GATE wins and the opt-in sentence is dropped.
6. GO-GATE-19 ('78 unclassified') vs GO-NET-09 and net conflict 12: GO-GATE-19 stays SHOULD and cites GO-NET-09's classification. The open question is closed.
7. GO-LANG-16 vs GO-OBS C9: GO-LANG-16 keeps the rule. The inverted nogreenteagc example is fixed and the grep is replaced with C9's watched form (3/3 red). GO-OBS-22 keeps the binary-side check.
8. perfsprint and prealloc (GO-OBS-17/18) vs GO-GATE-16: neither joins any fleet file, so the GO-GATE-16 roster is unchanged.
9. GO-MOD-14 vs GO-REL-14: consistent by scope. Both texts are kept, and GO-MOD-14 cites GO-REL-14.
10. go-bazel stale citations: the GO-REL-14 and GO-REL-05 references become GO-REL-06. BZL-GO-06's '5 analyzers go test runs' becomes 'the 5 analyzers rules_go vet=True names'.
11. GO-SEC-01's unanchored common-false-positives grep vs GO-GATE-09: GO-SEC-01 keeps its text and takes GO-GATE-09's anchored grep.
12. GO-IO-02 and GO-OBS-05 say 'G104/G115 only': GO-GATE-14 wins with G104, G115 and G304.

13. GO-LANG-04 check vs the toonew.go json/v2 exclusion: GO-LANG-04 keeps its rule. The durable check is the GO-MOD-16 oldstable build leg. golangci govet and nogo are named as not substitutes. A go-upgrade re-check is added.
14. GO-CONC-11 trigger vs GO-LANG-18: GO-CONC-11 keeps its text, and its grep gains -e 'iter\.Pull'.
15. Stale '11-analyzer' counts and GO-GATE-COMMANDS-* citations in the concurrency and testing files: these read '12 of 35' and cite GO-GATE-02.
16. GO-TEST-13's json/v2 caution stays dropped (wave-3 contradiction 16).
17. GO-CLI and GO-CONC YAML fragments: superseded by GO-GATE-22. Other families cite linter names and paste no YAML.
18. Open questions still listed in unrevised files but already answered (GO-SEC G7xx, GO-SEC G204 on CLIs, GO-TEST coverage scope): drafters omit them.
authoring_notes: N-1 Rules and globs: go-quality uses paths ["**/*.go"] with an index under 200 lines. go-modules uses these 13 quoted globs: **/go.mod, **/go.sum, **/go.work, **/go.work.sum, **/.golangci.*, **/*golangci*.yml, **/*golangci*.yaml, **/.goreleaser.*, **/goreleaser*.yml, **/goreleaser*.yaml, **/.config/goreleaser.*, **/.ko.yaml, **/staticcheck.conf. No brace globs. Run check-artifacts.py on the ko root with --allow-absent for go.work, go.work.sum, the dotless goreleaser names, .config/goreleaser.* and staticcheck.conf.

N-2 Depth files. go-quality gets language (GO-LANG), errors (GO-ERR), concurrency (GO-CONC), api-design (GO-API), testing (GO-TEST), cli-contract (GO-CLI), io (GO-IO), network (GO-NET), security (GO-SEC) and observability (GO-OBS). go-modules gets gates.md (GO-GATE) and release.md (GO-REL), and GO-MOD itself lives in the go-modules index. bazel-quality/go.md holds BZL-GO. Each file draws from its own consolidation plus the numbered (e) edits. Depth files never link to other depth files; they cite rule IDs only.

N-3 The go-quality index owns GO-CORE-01..05: never weaken a check; watch it red before trusting green; empty output means pass; read the go line first; generated code. The index also holds the gate block, a non-negotiables list of at most 25 lines with each line ending in its rule ID, the routing table by task, and Siblings. The 179 MUST rows stay in the depth tables. The go-modules index owns GO-MOD-01..18.

N-4 Bounded duplication: a rule's text appears once. The allowed repeats are the one-line index non-negotiables, GO-GATE-13's citation row, and the skill tables. Config YAML appears only in gates.md. The depguard list appears verbatim in the three config files and nowhere else.

N-5 Pins, each dated 'measured 2026-09-26': Go 1.27.1, golangci-lint v2.14.0, staticcheck 2026.2.1, gopls v0.23.0, cobra v1.10.1, goreleaser 2.17.1, cosign 3.1.3, Bazel 9.2.0, rules_go 0.63.0, gazelle 0.54.0, x/tools v0.50.0. Apply owner defaults Q1-Q8 and the (f) owner-default row, each written as a default the adopter may override. Project names (ocx, _dist.py, the SDK module path) appear only as examples the adopter renames.

N-6 Drop at authoring: GO-REL-13 (GO-API-10 wins; release.md keeps a one-line ID citation; the ID is never reused). GO-IO-18 (duplicates GO-NET-14; the ID is retired and the index routes blob staging to network.md). GO-GATE-13 stays a citation row only. Also drop GO-TEST-13's json/v2 caution, GO-API's line-63 opt-in sentence, the answered open questions, and the rejected dive claims (C7 stack allocation, 'config-assembly not landed', the CDN 403 stated as fact).

N-7 GO-NET-06 on ggcr: create ctx and cancel with context.WithCancelCause before remote.Layer or remote.Image, passing it via remote.WithContext, one per layer. The watchdog wraps the Compressed() reader and fires cancel. Cite image.go:154, layer.go:38-39 and fetcher.go:323, and mark the row 'wiring by source read, not fixture-watched'.

N-8 GO-LANG-04: the durable check is the GO-MOD-16 oldstable leg's go build ./..., and the fast check is bare go vet on 1.27.1. State in the rule that golangci govet and nogo are blind to this case because of x/tools v0.50.0 toonew.go:28-29.

N-9 Version dating: every version-specific claim names the tool and version and says '(measured 2026-09-26)' or '(read 2026-09-26)'. Each language floor says what gates it: the go line or the toolchain. Each depth file opens with one line listing the versions it binds to. Every upstream-issue gap links the issue and gives its state on 2026-09-26 (golang/go#74763, cobra#1708, bazel-gazelle#1797).

N-10 Verification-command shape: always pass an explicit directory operand. Use one -e per alternative, with no \| and no -E 'a|b' in a table cell. Quote --include and --exclude-dir globs. No unquoted **, no $(...), and no angle-bracket placeholders inside a pattern. Use xargs -r (or -0 -r). Never put an unescaped pipe in a table cell; piped commands go in a fenced block that the cell cites. Every cell states what empty output means: pass for a violation locator (grep exits 1), fail for a presence check. Every exit-code contract names its codes.

N-11 Skills: go-release, go-upgrade and go-diagnose are procedures only, as numbered steps that cite rule IDs. Any MUST a skill repeats goes in a '| # | Finding | Rule |' table, never in a row that starts with the rule ID. go-diagnose starts at GO-OBS-22.

N-12 go-upgrade dated re-checks, one step each: SA4023's test blind spot; the gosec empty-excludes pass including G304; config verify plus the superset check; the zap --fix probe; the roclose probe; the QF1009 probe; nojsonv2 and nogreenteagc removal; the go fix roster; gopls yield landing in vet or golangci (drop gate step 10 when it does); colorprofile NO_COLOR; the rules_go TOOLS_NOGO and nogo stdversion probe; buildvcs-r2/run.sh against #74763; the vendored toonew.go json/v2 exclusion.

N-13 bazel-quality/go.md: at most 200 lines, shaped like java.md. It needs frontmatter title and summary, an 'Owns BZL-GO' paragraph, sibling families cited but not restated, a Contents line, a measurement disclosure ('Measured 2026-09-26 against Bazel 9.2.0, rules_go 0.63.0, gazelle 0.54.0, Go 1.27.1'), a Gaps section and a 'What agents get wrong here' section. Frame it as 'if you adopt Bazel for Go'; it reopens bazel-topic-map.md:797 and has no glob of its own. In the same change: add one routing row to rules/bazel-quality.md; add keywords rules_go, gazelle, go_deps, nogo and x_defs; add go-quality and go-modules to Siblings and *.go to the 'never loads on' line; bump publish.toml [rules.bazel-quality] from 0.2.0 to 0.3.0; update docs/bazel-quality.md. Scope BZL-GO-14's byte-identity claim to linux_amd64.
N-14 Bundle go-essentials: go-quality, go-modules, go-release, go-upgrade and go-diagnose, all untagged. bazel-quality/go.md is not a member.
Depguard: GO-MOD-08 carries 13 entries (its 11, plus automaxprocs, plus x/exp/constraints), and the three fleet files re-quote them. Gate block: GO-GATE-01 gains conditional step 10 (gopls yield).
